# SEO-597: Do not mutate canonical or robots directives from client script

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Domain | `javascript-rendering` |
| Category | `TECHNICAL_SEO` |
| Minimum level | `LITE` |

| Confidence | `HIGH` |

## Statement

The canonical link and any index-controlling directive are written by the server render and are not added, removed, or rewritten by client code after the document loads.

## Rationale

A directive that only exists after script execution may never be observed, and one that changes after load leaves two different answers to the same question, with no way for the site to know which was read.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ],
  "any": [
    "client_rendered",
    "javascript_app"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Compute both values during the server render for every route, including routes reached through client navigation, and delete any client-side head manipulation that touches them. A client router changing the address must trigger a render that produces the correct values, not a patch applied to the previous document.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Compare the canonical link and index directives in the unexecuted response body against those present after load and after a client-side navigation.
- Evidence: `RAW_HTML`, `RENDERED_HTML`, `BROWSER`
- Automated check: `client-mutates-canonical`

## Scope

- Search surfaces: `GOOGLE_SEARCH`, `BING_SEARCH`
- Frameworks: `react-spa`, `vite`, `next-app-router`, `next-pages-router`, `astro`, `remix`, `sveltekit`, `nuxt`
- Caution: none recorded.
